newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-News Corp says Q1 below expectations.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-News Corp says Q1 below expectations.

text.p: News Corp Ltd chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch said on Tuesday the international media company's performance in the 1996/97 first quarter was below expectations.
Murdoch also told shareholders at the annual general meeting that the company continued to expect a rise of about 20 percent in full year earnings.
He said News Corp expected a strong year for its United Kingdom newspapers.
"We still expect to report an earnings rise of 20 percent this year, but the first quarter may not be up to that," Murdoch said. "But we expect to make up that shortfall."
He said the international paper shortage and the subsequent rise in paper prices which the company experienced in 1995/96 had eased and should not have a bottom line impact this year.
"We expect a strong year from the U.K. newspaper business."

Murdoch said the German pay television joint venture, through the company's BSkyB operation, should not have the same start-up problems experienced by its British pay television group, citing the larger German market and greater competition in Britain.
He said the German digital joint venture was expected to be profitable in about two to three years.
BSkyB, in which News Corp has 40 percent, would go digital by the end of calendar 1997 with 150 channels and computer-services such as home banking compared with current 28 channels, Murdoch said.
In late August, News Corp reported a six percent fall in 1995/96 (July/June) net profit before abnormals to A$1.26 billion.
At the time, Murdoch also forecast that the hit-film Independence Day would help the company achieve a 20 percent rise in 1996/97 earnings.
News Corp shares were steady at A$7.34 at 11.10 a.m. (0110 GMT), three cents below their opening price.
